newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes turn lower with few ANS bids.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes turn lower with few ANS bids.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices turned moderately lower midday Monday, with no buyers in the market for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude and sellers expecting little interest until after the holidays.
ANS's discount remained $1.70 a barrel off WTI more than a week after the last deal got done.
Outright ANS prices, reacting to flat diffs and soft WTI, were 25 cents lower than Friday at $24.05/24.25 a barrel.
Line 63 crude was also lower at $22.60/22.90 a barrel, but no deals were seen on a fixed basis and premiums stayed $0.95 to $1.05.
Kern River prices stayed at $18.65/18.75 a barrel after companies lifted postings late last week.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
Wilmington crude, produced offshore in Long Beach, Calif., also was flat at $20.15/20.25 a barrel.
